title: The Foolish Old Man Who Moved the Mountains
text:
North of two great mountains, Taihang and Wangwu, lived a man called Yu Gong, the Foolish Old Man, who was nearly ninety. The mountains blocked the way from his house to the south, and every journey meant a long detour.

He gathered his family and proposed that they level the mountains. His wife doubted it: he could not even flatten a small hill, and where would they put all the earth and stones? The family decided to carry them to the shore of the Bohai Sea. Yu Gong, his sons and grandsons began breaking rocks and digging soil and hauling it away in baskets. A neighbor's young son, a boy of seven or eight, skipped along to help. A round trip took a whole season.

A man known as the Wise Old Man of the River Bend laughed at him. At his age, he said, he could not even pull up a blade of grass on the mountain.

Yu Gong sighed. "When I die, my sons will carry on. They will have sons, and those sons will have sons, without end. But the mountains will not grow any higher. Why can't they be leveled?" The wise man had no answer.

According to the story, the spirit of the mountains heard this and reported it to the Lord of Heaven, who was so moved that he had the two mountains carried away.
lesson: Work that is too big for one lifetime can still be done by a family that shares the goal across generations. Start the work, and teach the next generation why it matters.
people: Yu Gong, his family, Zhisou (the Wise Old Man of the River Bend)
date: c. 4th century BC to 4th century AD
caveat: The Liezi's date is disputed, with many scholars placing its compilation around the 4th century AD.
